title: AI Stocks Dropped After the Election. Here’s Why I Think It’s Overdone
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Couch Investor argues the post-midterm sell-off in AI stocks is overdone. The Democrats winning the House and Senate changes nothing about data-centre build-out, he says, and the earnings evidence points the other way: AMD reported a strong quarter and guided to over 80% growth in fiscal 2027, close to $100 billion of revenue, while Nvidia's growth is still accelerating. He plays a clip from Howard Marks on tuning out short-term noise and sticking to the long-term story. He also covers Uber's strong quarter, with bookings up 20%, trailing-twelve-month free cash flow of $10.4 billion and a forward P/E of 17.8x, which he reads as cheap for the growth. AMD is up about 120% year-to-date, so he is not adding at these levels and sees Nebius, Broadcom, Nvidia, Meta and Google as better risk/reward, but he keeps his large AMD position. On Nebius he stays extremely bullish ahead of its report and guidance next week, possibly including a 2027 ARR number, while warning GPU pricing a year out will look very different. Calls: AMD HOLD (reiterated), NBIS BUY (first clear stance, was UNCERTAIN), UBER UNCERTAIN (positive read, no instruction).
